subject.title: Bound plugin bundle command file reads with size cap

question: Should installed Claude bundle-command Markdown files have a hard 1 MiB compatibility limit, with larger pre-existing commands skipped at load time after a warning?
rationale: The patch is mechanically narrow and proven, but the cap creates a new rejection boundary for third-party installed plugin content; repository policy treats plugin loader contract changes as compatibility-sensitive, and source/tests do not establish that 1 MiB is the intended product limit.

options.title: Accept the 1 MiB contract
options.body: Merge with the existing warning and continuation behavior, treating bundle commands above 1 MiB as unsupported installed content.

options.title: Choose a different documented limit
options.body: Keep the bounded-reader approach but set a limit that the plugin owner can support as the durable bundle-command contract.

options.title: Defer this cap
options.body: Leave current behavior unchanged until bundle-command size policy is specified through the plugin contract or documentation.

recommendation.title: Accept the 1 MiB contract
recommendation.body: Merge with the existing warning and continuation behavior, treating bundle commands above 1 MiB as unsupported installed content.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR is assigned to steipete, who also authored the follow-up commits that define the observable rejection behavior.
